question: What is the primary role of the Primary Health Care system within the broader health sector?

options.A: Regulating medical licensing and professional ethics
options.B: Acting as the first point of contact for health services
options.C: Managing tertiary medical research and clinical trials

explanation: PHC is structured to be the initial entry point for individuals seeking healthcare within the community. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary skill mix particularly vital for staffing primary health facilities?

options.A: It allows primary clinics to function strictly like tertiary hospitals
options.B: It prevents health workers from ever needing continuous training
options.C: It eliminates the need for any community volunteer involvement
options.D: It ensures a wide variety of basic health needs can be met locally

explanation: Because primary care deals with diverse community health issues ranging from maternal care to infectious diseases, a mix of skills is essential. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which facility represents the highest tier of the Primary Health Care system in Nigeria?
explanation: The Comprehensive Health Centre operates round-the-clock and provides advanced primary care services, including minor surgeries and admissions. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h2)

question: What staffing difference distinguishes a basic Health Post from a Comprehensive Health Centre?

options.A: Health Posts lack the multidisciplinary team and medical officers found in CHCs
options.B: Health Posts require more laboratory scientists than primary clinics
options.C: Health Posts operate twenty-four hours with intensive care units
options.D: Health Posts are exclusively staffed by medical consultants and surgeons

explanation: Health posts are smaller facilities managed primarily by lower cadres like CHEWs, whereas CHCs require medical officers, midwives, and specialized technicians. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which cadre at the primary health facility is primarily responsible for coordinating facility activities and linking with local health authorities?
explanation: CHOs hold supervisory and administrative responsibilities at the clinic level, acting as the administrative head in many primary health facilities. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h3)

question: A pregnant woman presents to a primary health clinic showing signs of obstructed labor. Which team member is best positioned to lead her immediate clinical assessment and stabilization before transfer?
explanation: Midwives and nurses possess the core competencies for managing obstetric assessments and identifying complications requiring urgent referral. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of establishing staffing norms and standards in primary healthcare?

options.A: To ensure equitable distribution and appropriate skill mix across facilities
options.B: To limit the total number of working hours for rural nurses
options.C: To guarantee that every health post has a resident medical surgeon
options.D: To restrict the employment of community health workers nationwide

explanation: Staffing norms provide a benchmark to prevent severe shortages and ensure facilities have the right personnel for their population size. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why do many primary health facilities fail to meet national staffing norms in everyday practice?

options.A: National guidelines forbid hiring any health personnel at the local level
options.B: All health workers automatically retire after five years of service
options.C: Primary health clinics have higher patient volumes than tertiary teaching hospitals
options.D: Geographical maldistribution and urban clustering of health workers

explanation: Health professionals frequently prefer urban postings due to better infrastructure, leading to severe rural deficits. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common human resource challenge in primary health care?

options.A: Internal and external brain drain of skilled personnel
options.B: Delayed salary disbursements and irregular promotions
options.C: Excessive availability of well-funded rural infrastructure

explanation: Rural infrastructure is notoriously deficient rather than excessively available, making this statement false. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h5)

question: How do poor living and working conditions in remote areas directly affect primary health service delivery?

options.A: They automatically increase government budgetary allocations to clinics
options.B: They drive staff turnover and absenteeism, leaving facilities short-handed
options.C: They eliminate all forms of inter-professional conflict among staff
options.D: They encourage health workers to remain indefinitely in rural posts

explanation: Unfavorable conditions cause workers to seek redeployment or abandon rural posts, resulting in compromised patient care. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is an example of a financial and infrastructural incentive designed to retain rural health workers?

options.A: Reducing the availability of basic working equipment
options.C: Providing rural hardship allowances and staff quarters
options.D: Eliminating all opportunities for professional promotion

explanation: Financial allowances and housing help offset the challenges of living in remote locations, improving retention. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h6)

question: A Local Government Health Authority wants to reduce high turnover among nurses in remote health posts. Which intervention should be prioritized first?

options.A: Provide secure staff housing and guaranteed regular allowances
options.B: Abolish the nursing supervisory roles at the facility level
options.C: Increase administrative paperwork for daily clinic attendance
options.D: Transfer all administrative meetings to distant urban state capitals

explanation: Addressing basic living security and financial recognition directly tackles the root causes of rural staff attrition. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the core philosophy of supportive supervision in primary healthcare management?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on financial auditing rather than clinical care
options.B: Punishing staff members immediately for every minor administrative error
options.C: Avoiding facility visits to prevent disturbing daily clinical routines
options.D: Mentoring frontline workers and solving operational problems collaboratively

explanation: Supportive supervision emphasizes guidance, mentorship, and joint problem-solving rather than mere punitive inspection. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h7)

question: Why are periodic in-service training and capacity building workshops essential for PHC personnel?

options.A: They are primarily used to evaluate personal political affiliations
options.B: They replace the need for initial basic professional qualifications
options.C: They ensure health workers never have to leave their workstations
options.D: They keep staff updated on evolving public health protocols and skills

explanation: Medical knowledge and public health guidelines evolve continuously; in-service training ensures staff competencies remain current. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h7)
